messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 2 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Band drift deep-dive & proposed ops playbook (sensitive calibration)

Team —

I pulled together a short analysis of the recent band drift we’re seeing across Eng infra and Platform PMs. Initial findings are attached (Q2_band_drift_analysis_v1.pdf) — the headline: median slot movement is +0.7 bands vs. expectations for this cycle, and variance is concentrated in two teams that overlapped with the April reorg.

Why I’m flagging this now:
- It’s showing up in the calibration panels as cross-team inconsistency (same role, different banding).
- Managers are asking for latitude to make corrective adjustments, but we don’t have a consistent process documented.

Proposed immediate actions (draft ops playbook attached):
1) Short-term: anonymized scorecard share + manager one-on-one calibration checklist (goal: consistent messaging).
2) HR guardrails: require People Ops approval for any band changes that affect comp baseline.
3) Escalation: create a transparent appeal route for impacted ICs.

Requesting: review the analysis and playbook for anything missing, and call out any blockers from HR or Comp perspective. I’d like to have a readout-ready one-pager for the Exec People sync on Tue.

Attachments: Q2_band_drift_analysis_v1.pdf, ops-playbook-draft.docx, team_scorecard_anonymized.csv

Thanks —
Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Head of People Analytics | Redwood Inference

Rishi —

Thanks for the thorough first pass. A couple quick notes from a calibration facilitator perspective:
- The anonymized CSV is helpful; please ensure manager-level IDs are removed before sharing more widely (we’ll need to avoid re-identification).
- Playbook step 1 should include a short script for managers to explain why we’re rechecking bands — transparency reduces appeals.

I can draft the one-pager for Exec if you share a 2–3 sentence topline I can pull into the slide. Also: can we surface potential comp impact ranges? Even a rough % change helps the CFO team.

Laura

Director, Talent Programs | Redwood Inference

Rishi / Laura —

Good work. A few pragmatic items from Managers Ops side:
- Playbook should include a "trusted reviewer" step where a non-involved manager reviews the proposed band move for bias checks.
- Timing: recommend a 10-business-day window for manager appeals to close the loop before comp refresh deadlines.
- Data request: I need the raw, anonymized distro per role (not per person) so my team can run a small normalization script. The CSV works but please redact manager emails.

Also — given this touches an external partner (Aurelia Health) pilot team, we need to coordinate any outward messaging. I’ve looped in Evelyn and Priya for HR/legal guardrails.

Marcus
Marcus Lin
VP, Manager Ops | Redwood Inference

Folks —

Appreciate the early thinking. A few HR constraints to call out before we standardize the playbook:
1) Any band change that moves an employee into a new comp band requires written consent from People Ops and a compensatory impact assessment (even if we do not change pay immediately).
2) For the Aurelia pilot: we must not disclose individual-level calibration outcomes externally. Messaging to partners should be at cohort level only.
3) Appeals: if an IC files an appeal that references performance management or discrimination, we must pause band adjustments until a formal HR intake is completed.

Priya — can you confirm if we need legal signoff on the script that managers will use? If yes, we should block 24–48 hours for review.

Evelyn
